basics.name: William Virgil Wolff
basics.label: IT Director / Systems Engineer
basics.summary: IT director and systems engineer with 12 years across networking, identity, physical security and infrastructure as code. Run a 4-person IT department for a multi-entity company: own the network, a Proxmox HA cluster and the M365 tenant, and ship internal software in Go and Laravel. Hands-on at every layer, from terminating fiber to writing the automation.

work.name: Grid-Line Transportation, Inc.
highlights: Lead a 4-person IT department (data analyst, full-stack developer, Tier 1 technician) for a 5-entity trucking group; hired and ramped the technician on a 90-day plan and five SOPs; launched an in-house service desk now used by every department head.

Primary maintainer and tie-breaker on a from-scratch transportation management system built with two other engineers (Laravel 13, Livewire 4, PostgreSQL 18, Octane, Horizon; 4,484 commits, 67 ADRs), in production beta since July 2026; solo-built the service desk and a QUIC remote-management tool (FastAPI, Go, React).

Built a 4-node Proxmox VE 9 HA cluster (2x R740xd, 2 NUC quorum nodes) with ZFS replication at a 5-15 minute RPO, proven on a real unplanned node fence; consolidated the legacy system from 4 chassis to 2 VMs, retiring 3 chassis and recovering 192 GB of RAM.

Redesigned the network on 2x UDM Pro Max: 11 VLANs under zone-based policy (275 rules), WireGuard site and client VPN, PowerDNS primary with two secondaries and split-horizon DNS, iDRAC and cellular WAN2 for out-of-band access; every firewall, DNS or hypervisor change carries a rollback point and two independent admin paths.

Owner's technical representative on a $1.4M HQ build-out: specified 87 Cat6 and 12 Cat6A drops, 12 Wi-Fi 7 APs, 19 cameras and 28 door readers before the walls closed; ran the low-voltage bid ($56.5K over $69K and $99K) and the 1 Gbps dedicated-fiber carrier bid; lighting design in DIALux, 121 fixtures.

Hardened the Microsoft 365 tenant: Global Admins 8 to 4, Intune and ASR conflicts to zero, 12 over-privileged Graph apps audited, former-MSP agents and AV removed fleet-wide, Bitwarden org rebuilt to least privilege, 11-secret credential rotation with zero lockouts.

Stood up a self-hosted platform (Vaultwarden, n8n, DocuSeal, Uptime Kuma, NetBox, MeshCentral with Azure-signed agents) behind Caddy and Entra SSO, a Warpgate bastion in place of Teleport, GitOps deploys with drift detection on a 20-runner CI fleet, and nightly offsite backups with restore drills.

Root-caused a silent 18-30% loss of driver load acceptances to a domain controller running 16 seconds ahead of NIST; after external NTP the loss went to zero. Nine n8n watches (~18K runs/month) now catch dispatch and assignment failures before drivers do.

Vendor decisions with real money: DocuSign to DocuSeal ($2.6K to ~$320/yr), Quo to Teams Phone on Telnyx direct routing (39 numbers to 3), Front to M365 (144 inboxes, 198 rules), lighting package renegotiated for a $30K material credit.

work.name: Team Solutions Group, LLC
highlights: First week: led ransomware recovery at Marmol Radziner (architects, 3 offices, every machine encrypted); regained domain control by booting Linux over iDRAC to reset a domain admin, led the wipe and rebuild of every workstation; staff working in a week, 40 TB restored in two.
Hardened it afterward (EDR, BitLocker, MFA, firewall) against the likely entry: a SonicWall VPN flaw, then an outside admin without MFA.

Donaldson (architects, 80 people, 3 offices): M365 E3/E5 down to Business Premium across a split M365/Google estate; benchmarked Core Ultra 7, 128 GB, RTX 4080 workstations for a firm-wide 3D-modeling refresh; scoped Proxmox to replace three Hyper-V hosts.
Project lead for a statewide CAL FIRE land-mobile-radio deployment (10 sites, 12 radios) and a 300+ room network overhaul (22 APs) at Best Western Plus, hitting compliance and uptime targets.

Built secure network and server environments for four Santa Barbara hotels (Brisas del Mar, Lemon Tree Inn, two Best Westerns): Microsoft 365, Azure, hybrid Active Directory and AD migrations, Intune and Jamf across Windows and macOS, VLANs, site-to-site VPNs.

Led identity projects for MSP clients (AD migrations, MFA rollouts, Global Admin audits) and mentored 5 junior engineers and service desk technicians; automated onboarding and offboarding in PowerShell.

work.name: Acelyrin, Inc.
highlights: Supported 180 users at a HIPAA-regulated biopharma (Entra ID with PIM just-in-time admin access, Microsoft 365 E3, Intune for 180 devices, Autopilot, Defender for Endpoint, 4 Zoom Rooms) at ~3-4 tickets/day.

Deployed 802.1X (EAP-TLS, Intune device certificates) for the managed fleet; ran HR-driven onboarding and offboarding with PowerShell Azure-vs-BambooHR identity reconciliation, plus SharePoint and Egnyte migrations.
Built Python API integrations to keep MATLAB data pipelines available to research analysts on demand.

work.name: SR Technologies
highlights: Managed 200+ network sites (~2/3 UniFi behind FortiGate firewalls) across hotels, theaters, warehouses and residential properties, including macOS and Windows support; led 5 direct reports and up to 6 outside low/high-voltage and general contractors.

Main point of contact for the largest client, Herbl, a California cannabis distributor (3 sites, 300+ computers, 500+ endpoints): Avigilon cameras and access control for the buildings and a ~50-vehicle delivery fleet on Cradlepoint, built to state cannabis retention rules.
Supported Herbl's SAP Business One integrations and user access, and the Zebra label printers behind state track-and-trace.

Delivered full-stack IT renovation of the post-acquisition La Quinta Inn by Wyndham (Santa Barbara): 1 MDF, 4 IDFs, 300+ guest rooms, bistro, back-of-house, multiple IP/vendor handoffs and servers, with end-to-end coordination across all trades.
Maintained 200+ access-control endpoints (strikes, maglocks) and CCTV/NVR systems on Verkada, UniFi, and Avigilon across all sites.

work.name: Ericsson
highlights: Serviced ~100 of 150+ cell towers from Malibu to San Luis Obispo; 1,000+ Cat5e/6/6e and coaxial terminations.
Administered CDMA, LTE, and 5G networks; installed multi-band antennas (800 MHz, 1900 MHz, 2.5 GHz) and managed Cisco, Juniper, and Lucent routers plus DAS/oDAS systems.

work.name: Sabrent
highlights: Managed 5 direct reports supporting a 50-person office, resolving ~7 tickets/day with sub-1-hour average response time.
Improved product reliability by leading firmware-update rollouts and investigating RMA returns to surface and resolve recurring quality issues.

work.name: NASO Corporation
highlights: Maintained IT and network for an aerospace/medical/defense electronics manufacturer under AS9100D and ISO 13485 compliance.
Cut operational costs by retiring legacy network gear and right-sizing infrastructure for the manufacturing and engineering staff.
